newsitem.title: USA: SIB report "cosmetic and avoids real issues" - NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: SIB report "cosmetic and avoids real issues" - NYMEX.

text.p: The UK's Securities and Investments Board's review has let LME off the hook and swept under the rug key unresolved issues thrown up by the Sumitomo affair, Neal Wolkoff, executive vice president of NYMEX said.

"The recommendations from my point of view are welcome, but they are purely cosmetic," Wolkoff said. "It takes a 19th century club and turns it into a 20th century club - it hasn't gotten to the fundamental issues."
"I could not imagine the Commodity Futures Trading Commission issuing such a report had Sumitomo happened here," Wolkoff said.
The LME called on the U.K. watchdog to review how the exchange operated amid criticisms following Sumitomo Corp's announcement in June of $2.6 billion losses from unauthorised copper trades.

NYMEX, whose COMEX division trades a rival copper futures contract, has been a persistent critic of LME since it opened copper warehouses in the U.S. more than a year before the Sumitomo scandal was revealed.

"Sumitomo did not occur because LME was without information about what Sumitomo was doing - it occurred because there was no appropriate margining system that highlighted to Sumitomo's management and to the world's clearing community the fact that this company was owing money on its positions," Wolkoff said.
Nevertheless Wolkoff welcomed the SIB's recommendation to review the LME's board to avoid conflicts of interest.
"This was the one thing that was definitely substantive," Wolkoff said.
Wolkoff was dismayed that the SIB appeared to have discussed the contents of its report with the LME prior to Thursday's publication.
The SIB said in a release that LME had agreed to take appropriate action, Wolkoff noted.
"If I were in the LME's shoes I would feel that if this is what it took to put an end to criticism, then I got off very very well," Wolkoff said.
NYMEX will let the SIB know about its responses to the review.
"This is really just sweeping something under the rug that does not deserve to be. It continues to be a looming issue for the financial community and hasn't been dealt with," Wolkoff said.
The LME has regularly dismissed NYMEX suggestions that the London exchange is less regulated than its New York rival.
